learning_outcomes.text: After successful completion, students can analyze and describe mechanical systems under motion and time-varying loads, and calculate forces and moments under dynamic conditions by learning to transform mechanical components and systems into dynamic models and to formulate and solve mathematical equations for these models, in order to address dynamic problems with engineering means and methods.

This includes the kinematics of a point and rigid bodies in translation, rotation, and general spatial motion, kinetics with free and guided motion, impulse, impact processes, center of mass, moment, and angular momentum theorems, energy methods with work and energy theorems, d'Alembert's principle and Lagrange's equations of the 2nd kind, as well as free and forced oscillations of linear oscillators.

Furthermore, students can evaluate parametric descriptions from Engineering Mechanics (Dynamics) and solve questions that cannot be solved analytically using numerical methods, by independently creating numerical descriptions for dynamic calculations and computing numerical solutions using relevant software (e.g. Matlab/Simulink, Octave, Python …).

syllabus_topics: Kinematics of rigid bodies: translation, rotation, general spatial motion
Numerical methods for integrating problems in point kinematics
Numerical calculation and representation of results from rigid body kinematics
Calculations and representations of results from relative kinematics
Numerical methods for solving ordinary differential equations and systems typical for mechanics dynamics
Center of mass theorem, moment theorem
Mass moment of inertia, Steiner's theorem, angular momentum
Kinetics of planar motion, Euler's gyro equations
Impulse and angular momentum theorems, simple impact processes
Work of conservative and non-conservative forces, potential, kinetic energy
Principles of mechanics: d'Alembert's principle, Lagrange's equations of motion 2nd kind
Free and forced oscillations of linear oscillators
assessment_rules: The module grade for MEXB320 is composed equally from "MECB321 Kinematics and numerical methods" and "MECB321 Kinetics" in a joint examination.
